evidence.title: Supplemental Information regarding Core Scientific, Inc., dated April 21, 2026
evidence.excerpt: Core Scientific's filing identifies Dalton 4 as a greenfield, one-building, three-data-hall development at 3024 Old Tilton Road, reports 145 MW of contracted critical IT capacity and 220 MW of secured grid capacity, and says its construction is being managed under a guaranteed-maximum-price contract.

metadata.status_scope: The filing calls Dalton 4 a greenfield development and says construction for Dalton 4 is being managed under an active construction contract with deadline-linked liquidated damages. Together with the later filing's current Dalton completion-progress update, this supports one generic under_construction observation and no finer physical substage.
metadata.critical_it_capacity_scope: The filing's project table labels 145 MW as Dalton 4 Critical IT Capacity, says the project set is contracted with CoreWeave, and separately assigns CoreWeave a 145 MW Dalton 4 power allocation under the Dalton 4 Colocation License Agreement. It is normalized once as contracted project critical_it_mw, not gross load, current draw, installed or energized capacity, grid capacity, generation, or annual energy.
metadata.grid_capacity_scope: The project table labels 220 MW as Dalton 4 Grid Capacity and the filing says grid capacity has been secured for the projects. It is normalized once as contracted project grid_connection_mw, not critical IT, gross facility demand, generation, current draw, annual energy, or measured consumption.
metadata.aggregate_capacity_guardrail: The 270 MW currently accessible to Dalton 1 and Dalton 4 in aggregate, 450 MW outside-provider aspiration, approximately 900 MW across five project sites, and approximately 590 MW cross-project critical IT total are not Dalton 4-only values and create no normalized rows. They are not allocated, summed, or used to modify the explicit Dalton 4 values.
metadata.may_update_capacity_guardrail: The later deck's approximately 175 MW Dalton leased-power figure aggregates the delivered 30 MW Dalton 1 site and the remaining Dalton program. It is not normalized or treated as Dalton 4 critical IT, grid connection, gross demand, current draw, or energy consumption.
metadata.role_scope: The filing says Core Scientific Finance, an indirect wholly owned Core Scientific subsidiary, is developing the six named facilities, including Dalton 4, and describes the restructuring of assets and rights required for their development and operation. The later Core Scientific deck explicitly describes its integrated developer and operator platform. These source-explicit statements support Core Scientific as developer and intended operator for Dalton 4, but no owner role is inferred from the ground lease or future restructuring.
metadata.coreweave_scope: The filing identifies a Dalton 4 Colocation License Agreement, says the facility set is 100% licensed to CoreWeave, assigns exactly 145 MW to Dalton 4, and grants CoreWeave use of purpose-built facilities for AI and HPC workloads. This supports CoreWeave only as the Dalton 4 tenant, one hyperscale_lease operating model, and ai_specialized_unspecified future workload. It creates no separate customer or user tag, current occupancy, installed hardware, accelerator, server, model, AI-training, or AI-inference observation.
